title: Game Theory
text:
0.1 Scope
These are lecture notes for Game Theory (third-semester elective, Master in Physics of Data, University of Padova). At the time of writing the professor has not yet distributed slides; this book is therefore a structural skeleton — chapter titles and a suggested organisation that will be filled in as the course progresses.
The skeleton follows the standard non-cooperative-then-cooperative curriculum:
Every chapter is currently a stub with a suggested table of contents.

title: Game Theory
text:
Chapter 1 — normal (strategic) form games; dominance and rationalisability.
Chapter 2 — Nash equilibrium in pure strategies.
Chapter 3 — mixed strategies and the existence theorem.
Chapter 4 — extensive-form games and backward induction.
Chapter 5 — games of incomplete information (Bayesian games).
Chapter 6 — cooperative game theory; core, Shapley value.
Chapter 7 — mechanism design and auction theory.

title: Game Theory
text:
0.2 Sources (planned)
Primary references: Osborne & Rubinstein, A Course in Game Theory, MIT Press (1994); Fudenberg & Tirole, Game Theory, MIT Press (1991); Myerson, Game Theory: Analysis of Conflict, Harvard University Press (1991).
